recent.title: US Chicago PMI (Oct)
recent.note: Miss: Chicago Barometer fell 3.5 points to 55.3 in October (prev 58.8), below the 56.0 WSJ consensus — activity cooling but still expanding; prices paid jumped to its highest since December 2021.

recent.title: US Employment Cost Index (Q3)
recent.note: Inline: Q3 ECI +0.8% q/q as expected, down from 0.9% — wages +0.7%, benefits +0.9%; labor costs cooling into the December decision, no fresh wage-inflation impulse (BLS, Oct 30).

recent.title: US GDP advance (Q3)
recent.note: Beat: Q3 advance 3.4% SAAR vs 3.2% consensus (prev 2.2%); consumer spending +3.8%, final sales +1.7% — the AI-capex quarter.

recent.title: US PCE price index (Sep)
recent.actual: Headline +0.5% m/m, +3.6% y/y; core +0.3% m/m, +3.1% y/y
recent.note: In line: September PCE matched forecasts; core y/y ticked up to 3.1% from 3.0% — sticky, not re-accelerating.

recent.title: US jobless claims (week ended Oct 24)
recent.actual: 194K (vs 198K fcst; prev week revised to 195K); continuing 1.701M (-21K)
recent.note: Beat: 194K vs 198K fcst (Reuters poll 199K); prev week revised to 195K; continuing claims 1.701M (-21K) — low-hire, low-fire intact.

recent.title: US advance goods trade balance + wholesale inventories (Sep)
recent.note: Miss: gap widened to $134.9B (Aug revised to -$132.1B) as imports +$8.1B outpaced exports +$5.3B; inventories +0.6% m/m beat +0.4% fcst, partly offsetting the drag. Census advance report CB26-177, Oct 28.

recent.title: German flash CPI (Oct)
recent.actual: +2.8% y/y (vs 3.1% HICP poll, prev 3.3%); CPI -0.2% m/m (vs 0.1% fcst, prev 0.6%); HICP +2.8% y/y; core 2.1% (prev 2.4%)
recent.note: Miss: German flash CPI cooled to 2.8% y/y (HICP 2.8% vs 3.1% poll, prev 3.3%), core 2.1% (prev 2.4%) — relief after the hot French (3.4%) and Italian (5.4%) flashes.

recent.title: Eurozone GDP (Q3 advance)
recent.note: Beat: Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q vs 0.2% expected, +1.3% y/y vs 1.1% — but Ireland's +5.5% flatters the headline; ex-Ireland growth ~0.2% (Eurostat, Oct 30). EUR/USD ticked up to ~1.1202 on the print.

recent.title: Eurozone unemployment rate (Sep)
recent.note: Miss: September jobless 6.5% vs 6.4% expected — though August was revised up to 6.5%, so no real deterioration (Eurostat, Oct 30).

recent.title: Italian prelim CPI (Oct)
recent.actual: +0.9% m/m (vs 0.1% fcst, prev 0.7%); +5.4% y/y (vs ~4.6% consensus, prev 4.2%)
recent.note: Sharp beat: Italian prelim CPI +0.9% m/m, +5.4% y/y vs ~4.6% consensus — the hot print in the eurozone flash batch (ISTAT, Oct 30).

recent.title: Italian GDP (Q3 advance)
recent.note: Miss: Italian Q3 GDP flat vs +0.1% expected — services and agriculture up, industry down, net exports a drag (ISTAT, Oct 30).

recent.title: German unemployment change (Oct)
recent.actual: +4K to 3.016M SA (vs 5K fcst, prev +12K); rate steady 6.4%
recent.note: Slight beat: German jobless rose 4K vs 5K expected, rate steady at 6.4% — but the labour office says conditions still don't support improvement (Oct 30).

recent.title: Nationwide house price index (Oct)
recent.actual: 0.0% m/m (vs -0.2% fcst; prev -0.2%, revised to -0.3%); +0.5% y/y (vs 0.6% exp, prev 0.8%)
recent.note: Beat: Nationwide house prices flat m/m vs -0.2% expected — but annual growth cooled to 0.5%, slowest since Jan 2024 (Nationwide, Oct 30).

recent.title: UK money and credit (Sep)
recent.actual: Approvals 53.4K (vs 54K fcst); net lending £5.8B (vs £6.2B); M4ex +4.0% y/y
recent.note: Miss: approvals 53.4K vs 54K fcst and below the ~58.8K six-month average; mortgage borrowing £3.9B (from £4.2B) and consumer credit £1.9B (from £2.7B) both down on August — credit cooling the morning after the Budget. Bank of England, Oct 29.

recent.title: BRC shop price index y/y (Oct)
recent.note: Beat: fastest shop-price rise since Feb 2024 — food 2.9% (Sep 2.5%), non-food 1.7% (Sep 0.8%); retailers passing on energy, transport and employment costs into Wednesday's Budget.

recent.title: CBI realized sales (Oct)
recent.note: Big beat: slowest retail fall since Apr 2025; orders -36 (vs -62 Sep); sterling eased anyway on pre-Budget positioning ($1.3348).

recent.title: UK flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.actual: Comp 53.1 (vs 51.8 fcst, Sep 52.0) — strongest since Feb; Mfg 52.8; Svc 53.1
recent.note: Beat: 53.1 vs 51.8 expected, strongest since February — demand resilience alongside the BoE repricing (Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: UK retail sales m/m (Sep)
recent.actual: -0.4% m/m (vs -0.1% fcst; Aug rev. up to +0.7%)
recent.note: Miss: -0.4% vs -0.1% expected — warm weather hit clothing and supermarkets; Aug revised up to +0.7% (ONS/Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: Japan housing starts y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Miss: starts swung from +6.1% to -2.7% y/y against expectations of a rise — construction cooling, but a low-impact print on BoJ morning; yen unmoved.

recent.title: Japan retail sales y/y (Sep)
recent.actual: 2.3% y/y (vs 3.3% exp, prev 2.9% revised from 2.7%); -0.7% m/m
recent.note: Miss: sales fell well short — household spending cooling into the BoJ; mixed read with the IP beat, yen unmoved.

recent.title: Tokyo CPI y/y (Oct)
recent.actual: Core 2.6% y/y (vs 2.6% exp, prev 2.7%); headline 2.8% (vs 2.7% exp)
recent.note: In line: core matched forecast at 2.6% while headline beat at 2.8% — December-hike case intact, no new signal into the BoJ.

recent.title: Japan consumer confidence (Oct)
recent.note: Slight miss: confidence eased to 35.0 from 35.4, just under the 35.1 forecast — households marginally more cautious into Friday's BoJ decision; not a yen mover on its own, with Tokyo CPI due Thursday night CT.

recent.title: Japan services PPI y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Inline: services PPI held at 3.7% y/y; ex-international-transportation eased to 2.9% from 3.2% — pipeline pressure steady, not accelerating, into Friday's BoJ decision.

recent.title: Japan flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.note: Manufacturing 53.3 (Sep 54.1) — 7-month low, miss vs 54.5 expected; services 52.0 (51.3) beat; composite 52.3 unchanged (19th straight expansion).

recent.title: KOF economic barometer (Oct)
recent.note: Miss: KOF barometer slipped to 107.6 vs 108.1 expected, from 109.1 — Swiss momentum cooling into the SNB's Dec 10 meeting (KOF, Oct 30).

recent.title: Swiss PPI m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Miss vs 0.6% fcst — disinflation intact; December SNB cut risk on the table.

recent.title: Australia PPI q/q (Q3)
recent.note: Slightly hotter: pipeline pressure still building into the RBA’s Nov 2-3 meeting, but a second-tier read beside Wednesday’s hot CPI.

recent.title: Australia private sector credit m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Beat on the monthly read but steady vs August’s pace — no fresh tightening or loosening signal into the RBA.

recent.title: Australia import prices q/q (Q3)
recent.note: Big miss: import prices fell 1.1% q/q vs 1.8% expected, reversing Q2's +5.7% surge; petroleum (-8.7%) and fertilisers (-20.2%) drove the drop as Hormuz shipping reopened. Pipeline pressure cooled even as Q3 CPI ran hot — a dovish wrinkle into the RBA's Nov 2-3 meeting, though the Aussie barely moved (near $0.7051).

recent.title: Australia CPI (Q3 + Sep)
recent.actual: Trimmed +1.0% q/q (vs 1.0% fcst; above RBA's 0.8% forecast); headline +1.3% q/q; monthly Sep headline 4.3% y/y (vs 4.2%)
recent.note: Inline vs consensus but hotter than the RBA's August path — Nov 2-3 hike odds jumped to ~79-85%; AUD spiked to $0.7053. ABS monthly trimmed 3.6% y/y vs calendar quarterly trimmed 3.7% y/y — different series, not blended.

recent.title: China loan prime rates (Oct)
recent.note: Inline: PBoC held LPR for the 17th straight month — neutral for the China-demand read.

recent.title: China Q3 GDP y/y (AUD demand read)
recent.note: Retail +1.1% the standout (2x fc); two-speed beat — factories lead, property -20.6% YTD. AUD best G10 performer.

recent.title: Canada GDP (Aug)
recent.note: Miss: August GDP flat vs +0.2% expected — the advance estimate's rebound did not materialize; loonie firmer anyway (USD/CAD ~1.3959 post-release) on the oil bid and the offered dollar (ActionForex, Oct 30; StatsCan text pending).

recent.title: Canada retail sales m/m (Aug)
recent.note: A tenth light: +1.2% vs +1.3% fcst (Jul -0.7%); ex-autos +1.2% beat vs +1.0%; Sep advance +0.7% — essentially inline, loonie unmoved near 1.40.

recent.title: Canada IPPI m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Beat: +2.0% m/m vs 0.7% fcst (Aug rev. to +1.2%) — +14.5% y/y, 24th straight annual gain; upstream pressure supports the hawkish BoC repricing.

recent.title: Canada raw materials price index m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Big beat: +4.8% m/m vs 0.1% fcst (prev 3.1%) — +27.0% y/y; raw-material costs surging alongside the IPPI beat.

recent.title: Canada new housing price index m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Slight miss: -0.2% m/m vs -0.1% consensus — second straight soft month; Toronto and Oshawa steepest annual declines (-4.9% y/y). Shelter drag continues into the BoC's Oct 28 deliberation.

recent.title: Canada CPI y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Mild miss: 3.1% vs 3.2% Reuters consensus (prev 3.0%) — keeps October-28 a ~1-in-4 maybe after the -68.3K jobs miss.

recent.title: NZ CPI (Q3) q/q + y/y
recent.note: Soft miss on both measures — 0.7% q/q vs 0.8% fcst (prev 1.5%), 3.7% y/y vs 3.8% (from 4.1%; RBNZ had projected 3.9%) — but still above the 1–3% target; NZD dipped to $0.5692; Oct-28 hike stayed ~98% priced (Reuters, Oct 22).

recent.title: Global Dairy Trade Event 414
recent.note: Beat: powder-led firm — WMP +4.4% to $3,760/t, SMP +3.4% — positive terms-of-trade read into the Oct-28 RBNZ.

recent.title: NZ trade balance (Sep)
recent.note: Miss: NZ$1.97B deficit vs NZ$0.78B fcst — fuel import prices +96% y/y did the damage, not volumes.

recent.title: NZ food price index m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Food prices flat vs +0.3% prior — softens the near-term inflation pulse into Oct 28.

recent.title: NZ BusinessNZ manufacturing PMI (Sep)
recent.note: 56.5 vs 53.1 prior — strongest since 2021; 15th straight expansion; employment back growing.
